areas.

notices.subject: [Routeing Change — Restricted Area Changes] BLACK SEA - BLACK SEA GRAIN INITIATIVE
notices.body:
BLACK SEA
BLACK SEA GRAIN INITIATIVE
JOINT COORDINATION CENTER (JCC) - ISTANBUL
182359Z MAR 23 UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE
DATUM WGS84.
THE BLACK SEA GRAIN INITIATIVE JCC HAS ESTABLISHED A ROUTE FOR VESSELS INBOUND AND OUTBOUND OF UKRAINAN PORTS. THE ROUTE IS 320NM LONG AND CONNECTS THE LISTED UKRAINIAN PORTS WITH INSPECTION AREAS INSIDE TURKISH TERRITORIAL SEAS.
THE MARITIME HUMANITARIAN CORRIDOR (MHC) FORMS PART OF THIS ROUTE AND EXTENDS FROM THE BOUNDARY OF UKRAINIAN TERRITORIAL SEAS TO THE SOUTHERN WAYPOINT OF THE HIGH SEAS TRANSIT CORRIDOR (HSTC).
WHILST TRANSITING THE MHC NO MILITARY SHIP, AIRCRAFT OR UAV MAY CLOSE WITHIN A RADIUS 10NM OF ANY VESSEL ENGAGED IN THE INITIATIVE AND TRANSITING THE CORRIDOR. VESSELS ENCOUNTERING PROVOCATIONS OR THREATS WHILE TRANSITING THE MHC SHOULD REPORT IMMEDIATELY TO THE JCC. NO VESSEL SHALL TRANSIT THE MHC WITHOUT THE AUTHORISATION OF THE JCC.
PILOTS WILL EMBARK FOR PASSAGE BETWEEN BERTH AND HOLDING AREA.
CHORNOMORSK TO HOLDING AREA. CHANNEL W

ISRAEL NOTICE TO MARINERS 060/2026
Anchorage Prohibited Area – Gas Pipeline Warning

Subject: Anchorage Prohibited Area – Gas Pipeline Warning
The Israeli Shipping and Ports Authority hereby warns all vessels that a significant number of subsea gas pipelines are laid along the Israeli coastline.
Vessels intended or instructed to anchor outside designated port anchorage areas must exercise extreme caution.
Please be advised that some recently laid gas pipelines may not yet be marked on official navigational charts.
It is required to follow relevant Port VTS or to consult nearby offshore platforms to verify that your intended anchorage position is completely clear of underwater hazards.
Continuous watch on VHF Channel 16 is mandatory for all vessels at all times.
Failure to respond to incoming calls from authorities will be considered clear grounds for a Port State Control (PSC) inspection and suspected violation of prohibited anchorage areas.

notices.body:
IN AREA BOUNDED BY:
4 AUGUST 2025
RESTRICTED AREA BETWEEN "PONTA TAL-AHRAX" AND "DAHLET IX-XILEP"
THE PORTS AND YACHTING DIRECTORATE, TRANSPORT MALTA, NOTIFIES THAT AS PART OF AN EU LIFE
PROJECT, AIMED AT PROTECTING THE YELKOUAN SHEARWATERS (GARNIJA), SEABIRDS THAT BREED
ON CLIFFS, A RESTRICTED AREA IS ESTABLISHED. ONE SUCH BREEDING AREA IS LOCATED AT "RDUM
TAL-MADONNA" ON THE CLIFFS BETWEEN IL-PONTA TAL-AHRAX AND DAHLET IX-XILEP.
THE HABITAT AND BREEDING GROUND OF TEN PER CENT (10%) OF THE WORLD'S POPULATION OF
YELKOUAN SHEARWATERS, IS LOCATED AT "RDUM TAL-MADONNA". THE AREA HAS BEEN
DESIGNATED AS A "SPECIAL PROTECTION AREA" (SPA) AND IS NOW OF INTERNATIONAL IMPORTANCE
AND INTEREST IN THE CONSERVATION OF THE SPECIES AND OF OTHER SEABIRDS. LIGHT AND NOISE
SERIOUSLY DISTURB THE BIRDS WITH THE DANGER OF THEM DESERTING THE COLONY.

notices.body:
22 OCTOBER 2026
CIRKEWWA MARINE PARK - SPECIAL MARKER BUOYS
UNRELIABLE AND NOT IN THEIR CHARTED POSITIONS
REFERENCE IS MADE TO BA CHART 211A - CHANNELS BETWEEN MALTA AND GHAWDEX
THE PORTS AND YACHTING DIRECTORATE, TRANSPORT MALTA, NOTIFIES MARINERS THAT THE
FIVE SPECIAL MARKER BUOYS WITHIN THE CIRKEWWA MARINE PARK ARE CURRENTLY
UNRELIABLE AND MAY NOT BE IN THEIR CHARTED POSITIONS.
MARINERS ARE ADVISED THAT THESE BUOYS, EXHIBITING A YELLOW FLASHING LIGHT (FL.Y.5S),
MAY HAVE SHIFTED FROM THEIR DESIGNATED LOCATIONS. CONSEQUENTLY, THE BUOYS
SHOULD NOT BE RELIED UPON FOR NAVIGATION.
THE AFFECTED BUOYS ARE CHARTED IN THE FOLLOWING POSITIONS:
LATITUDE (N) LONGITUDE (E) FLASHING
35-58.236N 014-18.881E FL. Y.5S
35-58.343N 014-18.474E FL. Y.5S
35-58.587N 014-18.658E FL. Y.5S
35-58.769N 014-18.795E FL. Y.5S
35-59.052N 014-19.009E FL. Y.5S
ARE UNRELIABLE AND NOT IN CHARTED POSITIONS
MARINERS ARE THEREFORE REQUESTED TO NAVIGATE WITH EXTREME CAUTION WHEN
TRANSITING OR CONDUCTING DIVING OPERATIONS WI

HERITAGE ACT (CAP. 445).

notices.subject: [Security Requirement Change] EASTERN CARIBBEAN SEA - ST. KITTS AND NEVIS - SABA BANK HAS BEEN DESIGNATED AS AN IMO
notices.body:
EASTERN CARIBBEAN SEA.
ST. KITTS AND NEVIS.
1. SABA BANK HAS BEEN DESIGNATED AS AN IMO
 ADOPTED AREA TO BE AVOIDED (ATBA) AND
 PARTICULARLY SENSITIVE SEA AREA (PSSA). 
2. TO AVOID THE RISK OF POLLUTION AND DAMAGE
 TO THE ENVIRONMENT, ENTRY IS PROHIBITED FOR
 VESSELS OF 300 GROSS TONS AND GREATER, AND
 ANCHORING IS PROHIBITED FOR ALL VESSELS,
 IN AREA BOUND BY
 17-27.06N 063-56.14W, 17-29.00N 063-55.09W,
 17-27.94N 063-43.32W, 17-38.03N 063-27.41W,
 17-43.35N 063-32.74W, 17-45.98N 063-29.98W,
 17-40.34N 063-21.10W, 17-30.88N 063-10.92W,
 17-23.80N 063-11.25W, 17-16.27N 063-15.85W,
 17-13.44N 063-26.89W, 17-10.55N 063-41.81W,
 17-20.85N 063-49.89W.
 VESSELS VIOLATING THESE REGULATIONS WILL
 RECEIVE A FINE.
3. FOR FURTHER INFORMATION, CONTACT DUTCH
 CARRIBEAN COAST GUARD, PHONE: 599 9463 7620,
 599 9510 0913, EMAIL: RCC.CURACAO@MINDEF.NL.
4. CANCEL NAVAREA IV 1518/24.

notices.category: Navigational Warning — New or Amended Regulation
notices.subject: [Navigational Warning — New or Amended Regulation] Southern Gulf & Gulf of Oman: Oman Transit Instructions – Strait of Hormuz
notices.body:
Southern Gulf & Gulf of Oman: Oman Transit Instructions – Strait of Hormuz
BA Charts 2837, 2851, 2858, 2888, 3172, 3174.
Oman Charts OM1219, OM1218.
Due to the existing risks along the current Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS) in the Strait of Hormuz, and
to ensure secure and safe of navigation in this important waterway, the Sultanate of Oman in
coordination with the IMO, has issued important guidance and instructions for vessels planning to transit
the Strait without the imposition of any tolls.
Temporary alternative routes have been established at the north and south of the TSS, together with a
safe waiting area within a 3 Nm radius of position 26-16.17N/055-46.52E near the strait.
All vessels are therefore advised to review this guidance prior to transiting the Strait. The details have
been promulgated through SafetyNET in Bulletin No. 208-2026, issued by the Pakistan Navy, and can be
accessed through the MENAS website using the link below.
https://menas.bh/wp-content/uploads/OMAN-IN

notices.subject: [Navigational Warning] Strait of Hormuz - Attack
notices.body:
Incident Date: 11 Nov 2026  Incident Time: 1800UTC

UKMTO has received a time-late report of an incident 14NM northwest of Ra’s al Khaymah, UAE.
A tanker was struck by an unknown projectile in the engine room.
No casualties have been reported and all crew have been evacuated safely.
Fire-fighting efforts are currently ongoing.
Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO, whilst authorities investigate.

Position: 25-58.00N 055-46.00E

notices.region: Navigational Warning (Red Sea / Gulf of Aden / Persian Gulf)
notices.subject: [Navigational Warning] Southern Arabian Gulf - Attack
notices.body:
Incident Date: 10 Nov 2026 Incident Time: TBC
UKMTO has received a time-late report of an incident in the Arabian Gulf.
A tanker has been struck by an unknown projectile whilst travelling eastbound.
Multiple casualties were sustained and have been taken ashore for medical assistance.
All remaining crew are safe and accounted for.
No damage assessment or environmental impact are available at this time.
Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO, whilst authorities investigate.

Position: 25-25.00N 053-35.00E

notices.region: Navigational Warning (Red Sea / Gulf of Aden / Persian Gulf)
notices.subject: [Navigational Warning] Strait of Hormuz - Suspicious Activity
notices.body:
UPDATE 001
UKMTO has received a report of an incident involving a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz.
The status of crew, damage assessment, and environmental impact are unknown at
the time of this report.
UPDATE 001: UKMTO have now gained confirmation that the tanker was struck with an unknown projectile whilst transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
All crew are reported safe and well.
Due to this confirmation, this has been re-classified as an Attack.
Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to
UKMTO, whilst authorities investigate.

notices.region: Navigational Warning (Red Sea / Gulf of Aden / Persian Gulf)
notices.subject: [Navigational Warning] Strait of Hormuz - Attack
notices.body:
UKMTO has received a time-late report of an incident 16NM east of Khasab, Oman.
The Master of a Tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz outbound, has reported an
explosion at the waterline, port side. The crew are safe and are accounted for. The
tanker is still under its own power and is continuing on its voyage.
Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO,
whilst authorities investigate.

Position: 26-10.00N 056-32.00E

The Naval Undersea Warfare Center (NUWC) at Keyport, WA is continuing operations in vicinity of NUWC between University Point, the Brownsville Marina and Keyport through 23 Dec 2026. Operations will normally be conducted Monday through Friday during daylight hours. Operations will involve semisubmersible and submersible vehicles escorted by a small naval craft with a flashing red light. The small craft will monitor VHF-FM channels 12 and 16. The call sign for the small craft will be “Keyport Range Control”. All craft transiting the area are requested to exercise caution and maintain a sharp lookout for possible semi-submerged vehicles while the range is in operation. Questions can be directed to Keyport Range Control on VHF-FM channels 12 and 16 or by contacting the Pacific Northwest Range Management and Ops Division, Range Control Branch, at (360) 396-2313.

Waterway information - ECHO Program
HARO STRAIT AND BOUNDARY PASS – ECHO Program 2025 Voluntary Ship Slowdown 
Effective June 15 to November 30, 2026 the ECHO Program voluntary ship slowdown through Haro Strait and Boundary Pass is active for all inbound and outbound commercial and government vessels to reduce underwater noise for at-risk whales. This initiative will remain in effect 24 hours per day until 2359 PDT on November 30, 2026, depending on southern resident killer whale presence in the fall. If it is safe and operationally feasible to do so, commercial and government vessels are requested to not exceed the following speeds through the water: 
11 knots – Bulkers, tankers, general cargo vessels, and government vessels; and, 
14.5 knots – Vehicle carriers, cruise ships, and container vessels.

notices.region: Navigational Warning — Restricted Area Changes (NE Pacific / US West Coast / Alaska / Hawaii)
notices.subject: [Navigational Warning — Restricted Area Changes] Waterway information
notices.body:
Waterway information
Effective 0700 UTC JUN 1 2026, to comply with the Interim Order for the Protection of Southern Resident Killer Whales (Orcinus orca) in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026, vessels must not approach within a distance of 1000m of a Southern Resident Killer Whale in the Southern Resident Killer Whale critical habitat and British Columbia coastal waters east of Vancouver Island and south of Campbell River (Cape Mudge) and Ucluelet, including Barkley Sound (up to Port Alberni) and Howe Sound, with coordinates listed in Schedule 1 of the Interim Order.
These prohibitions are in effect until May 31st, 2027. Details of vessel exceptions from the approach distance are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 3(2), and 4(2) of the Interim Order. Note that vessels in transit are excepted from the approach distance measure.

Notice is hereby given to all mariners operating in the Pacific Coast that, according to the report from the Costa Rican Institute of Pacific Ports (INCOP) via official letter CR-INCOP-DOP-2026- 00118, discrepancies have been detected in the aids to navigation (AtoN) system. Mariners are advised to exercise extreme caution, maintain a sharp visual lookout, and reinforce instrumental navigation (GPS, radar, and echo sounder) when transiting these areas:
1. Golfito approach channel buoy (starboard hand, red), position 08° 37' 47.28" N 083° 10' 06.55" W, light system damaged / unlit.
2. Golfito approach channel buoy (starboard hand, red), position 08° 37' 47.05" N 083° 09' 57.74" W, light system damaged / unlit.
3. Puntarenas Pier buoy (starboard hand, red), position 09° 58.309' N 084° 49.917' W, light system damaged / unlit.
Source: CR-INCOP-DOP-2026-00118

COSTA RICA NOTICE TO NAVIGATORS 032/2026
Notice to mariners operating along the Pacific Coast are hereby advised that, according to report CR-INCOP-DOP-2026-00214 issued by the Costa Rican Institute of Pacific Ports (INCOP), disruptions have been detected in the visual aids to navigation system. Extreme visual lookout and reinforced instrument navigation (GPS, radar, and echo sounder) are recommended when transiting the following areas:
1. Buoy No. 1 – Punta Morales Access Channel (Red): Located at 9° 57.591' N, 84° 52.654' W, has been stolen.
2. Buoy No. 2 – Punta Morales Access Channel (Red): Located at 10° 01.075' N, 84° 56.337' W, has been stolen.
3. Buoy No. 3 – Punta Morales Access Channel (Red): Located at 10° 02.880' N, 84° 58.464' W, has been stolen.
4. Quepos Lighthouse (White Light): Located at 9° 37' 39.0" N, 84° 40' 29.6" W, is malfunctioning and currently out of service.
Source: CR-INCOP-DOP-2026-00214 (September 01, 2026).

notices.subject: [Special Operations] Mariners are hereby advised that, according to information received from authorities in Panama and the United States, an aerostatic bal
notices.body:
COSTA RICA NOTICE TO NAVIGATORS 022/2026
Mariners are hereby advised that, according to information received from authorities in Panama and the United States, an aerostatic balloon reportedly suffered an explosion and subsequently fell into the sea in waters of Costa Rica. As a result of the incident, debris and wreckage may be present on or near the surface of the sea, potentially posing a hazard to navigation. All vessels navigating in the area are therefore advised to exercise extreme caution, maintain a proper lookout, and proceed at a safe speed, due to the possible presence of floating debris. Approximate reported position: 09°58'39.25"N – 086°12'40.32"W Approximate distance from the coastline: 37 nautical miles, as indicated on the attached chart. Mariners are requested, upon sighting any debris or wreckage possibly associated with this incident, to avoid approaching the objects when practicable and immediately report the position and any relevant information to the appropriate

notices.body:
COSTA RICA NOTICE TO NAVIGATORS 004/2026
Mariners operating along the Pacific Coast are hereby advised that the sailboat "AURIGA" has sunk at coordinates 08°36'40" N, 083°08'57" W, approximately 100 meters off the beach in the INVU sector of Golfito. At high tide (pleamar), the vessel is almost completely submerged, with only about 50 centimeters of its mast remaining visible above the water. As the wreck is currently unmarked and lacks any maritime signaling, all vessels are urged to exercise extreme caution and maintain a sharp lookout when navigating near the specified area.
Source: DVMP-DNS-CP-PG-2026-84, Capitanía de Puerto de Golfito
Document: https://www.mopt.go.cr/sites/default/files/destacados/maritimo/avisos-navegantes/pacifico/2026/mopt-04-04-22-004-2026-precaucion-navegacion-velero-hundido-golfito.pdf

notices.region: Routeing Change (Arctic / Greenland / Northern Passages)
notices.subject: [Routeing Change] Routeing Change - North Atlantic Right Whale
notices.body:
Routeing Change - North Atlantic Right Whale
Effective 241500 UTC Oct 2026, the following North Atlantic Right Whale restriction Zones are in effect for all vessels greater than 13 meters in length overall:
Static Zones North and South: Vessels must not exceed 10 knots over ground.
Dynamic Shipping Zones A, B, C, D, and E: No restriction in effect.
Seasonal Management Areas 1 and 2: No restriction in effect.
Restricted area: No restriction in effect.
Voluntary Seasonal Slowdown: Vessels are requested to reduce their speed less than 10 knots over ground.
Additional details are available in Notices to Mariners. Failure to comply with speed restrictions in effect can lead to enforcement action by Transport Canada.
Mariners are requested to report whale sightings and observations of entangled, dead, or injured whales to Marine Communication and Traffic Services.

notices.subject: [Communication or Broadcast Service Change] Waterway information - Calculation of under-keel clearance
notices.body:
Waterway information - Calculation of under-keel clearance
Canadian Coast Guard Marine Communications and Traffic Services have been using all Canadian Hydrographic Service water-level stations for the calculation of passage authorizations in the SorelMontreal sector of the navigational waterway, namely Sorel, Contrecoeur, Varennes, Montreal-Frontenac and Montreal-Jetty No. 1.

In light of the particular features of the navigational waterway in the portion between buoys M84 (downstream of the municipality of Verchères) and M11 (downstream of the Bellmouth curve), it was agreed to adjust upward the available water column by 10 cm in this portion.

The minimum water column in this portion of the navigational waterway as per the Contrecur hydrographic station, obtained after adjustment, will be used for the calculation of under-keel clearance.

POSITION 45-47.287N 073-20.935W
POSITION 45-56.548N 073-12.668W

notices.subject: [Communication or Broadcast Service Change] Waterway information - Calculation of under-keel clearance
notices.body:
Waterway information - Calculation of under-keel clearance
Canadian Coast Guard Marine Communications and Traffic Services have been using all Canadian Hydrographic Service water-level stations for the calculation of passage authorizations in the SorelMontreal sector of the navigational waterway, namely Sorel, Contrecoeur, Varennes, Montreal-Frontenac and Montreal-Jetty No. 1.

In light of the particular features of the navigational waterway in the portion between buoys M84 (downstream of the municipality of Verchères) and M157 (opposite to the Port of Montreal, section 109) as well as the No. 1 Anchorage Pointe-aux-Tremble, it was agreed to adjust upward the available water column by 10 cm in this portion.

The minimum water column in this portion of the navigational waterway as per the Varennes hydrographic station, obtained after adjustment, will be used for the calculation of under-keel clearance.

Monthly Notice to Mariners Eastern Edition 08/22 refers.
